message.content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "cross_validate_history_with_radiographic_distribution", "description": "When clinical history suggests a specific etiology (e.g., trauma) but radiographic findings follow a different anatomical pattern (e.g., gravity-dependent), verify if the visual distribution matches the proposed mechanism before concluding.", "applicable_conditions": "Tasks involving medical imaging interpretation where there is a discrepancy between the patient's clinical history and the anatomical distribution of radiographic findings.", "branch": "task_level", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["medical_imaging_interpretation"], "required_tools": [], "risk_level": "high", "core_action": "If the radiographic findings (e.g., opacities, fractures, effusions) do not align with the expected anatomical distribution of the pathology suggested by the clinical history: (1) explicitly identify the anatomical pattern of the visual findings (e.g., gravity-dependent vs. site-of-impact); (2) compare this pattern against the mechanism of injury or disease process implied by the history; (3) prioritize the diagnosis that best explains the specific radiographic distribution, even if it contradicts the initial historical impression."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
